title: Bijectivity of a single-coordinate flip
statement: Fix $n \in \bbn$ and a coordinate $i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,n$. On the space of $n$-bit Boolean inputs, functions $\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \mathrm{Bool}$, consider the single-coordinate flip that negates the $i$-th bit of its argument and leaves every other bit unchanged. This map is a bijection.
replaced:
For every $i : \mathrm{Fin}\,n$, the map
$\texttt{flipAt}\,i : \texttt{BoolInput}(n) \to \texttt{BoolInput}(n)$ is bijective; its
two-sided inverse is itself.
